5. Tahsildar, Tahsil Bilha, District Bilaspur Chhattisgarh  ---- Respondents (Cause-title taken from Case Information System) For Petitioners : Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pandey,
Advocate For Respondents/State : Shri Sudhir Sahu, PL Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18015 Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order On Board 19/07/2023 1.

The present writ petition has been filed by the petitioners and prayed for the following reliefs:
"10.1.

That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a suitable writ or writ for directing the respondents authorities to give the compensation amount along with interest to the petitioners in accordance with law or give the land to the petitioner No.1.
10.2 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue any other relief, as may be deemed fit and proper by this Hon'ble Court in the facts and circumstances of the case."

2. The issue raised in this petition has come up for consideration before the Division Bench of this Court in W.P.C. No.7048/2007 decided on 30.11.2018 wherein it has been held as under:
"42.

If the petitioners' forefathers became bhumidhari under the MPLRC, 1954 there is absolutely no reason why their forefathers orafter their demise the present petitioners did not more application for conferral of bhuswami rights under Section 150 of the MPLR, 1954 or the CGLRC, 1959 for last about seven decades.
There is no proof that the petitioners or their forefathers had ever paid the land revenue under Section 148 of the MPLRC, 1954.

As a matter of fact, this provision by itself exposes the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18015 fallacy in the petitiops' argument because a bhumidhari is required to pay the same land revenue, which he was paying rent in respect of lands held by him.
It is the petitioners' owncase and it is the case of all Kotwars who were enjoying service land before coming into force the CGLRC,1959 that they were exempte from payment of land revenue.

43. For all the above reasons, we are of the considered view that Lalla Singh Chouhan & Others of 2014 decided on 01.02.2018) has not laid down the correct law and the finding that lands held by Ex- Kotwars as a grant from malguzar would be saved to them as Bhumiswami land is erroneous particularly in view of the prolvisions of Section 3 of the Abolition Act, 1950 read with Sections 147,148 and 150 of the MPLRC, 1954.

Resultantly, the orders/judgments in the matters of Chhabil Das &
Others Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh an Another (WP No. 2632 of 2000 decided on 30.10.2001), Tikaram & Others Vs.
